experiment: FLUX.2 Klein 4B Mira whole-shot generalization matrix
fixed_method: Diffusers Flux2KleinPipeline, public BF16 model, sequential CPU offload, 4 inference steps, guidance scale 1.0

gates.variables: subway stair descent; camera one step below at knee height; large foreground shoe
gates.evidence: All outputs show a full body, visible upward camera direction, enlarged foreground shoe, stair perspective, walking pose, and the Mira costume/bag contract.

gates.variables: true left-side profile; rainy pedestrian crossing; city bus background
gates.evidence: All outputs show a full side profile, walking pose, readable city setting, and the Mira hair, clothing, shoes, bag, and single strap.

gates.variables: 768x1152 full body; both hands holding a ticket at chest height
gates.evidence: Faces, eyes, visible hands, ticket contact, and full body are readable. The watercolor-reference result changes the required rectangular flap bag into a non-flap bag, so it is rejected.

gates.variables: 45-degree rear-left view; face contour visible; riverside promenade
gates.evidence: The male-webtoon and text-only results preserve one bag and one strap. The Mira-reference result creates two bag bodies; the watercolor-reference result creates two crossing straps.

conclusion: Natural-language camera constraints can produce low-angle and side full-body cuts without OpenPose. Direct reference conditioning is not yet sufficient for rear-view prop consistency. Only an output that passes the whole-shot bag/strap gate may proceed to local inpainting.
